processing.name: Hooghly River Industrial Corridor (West Bengal)
products: Strategic Role: The global manufacturing center for woven jute products. Runs along both banks of the Hooghly river through Howrah, Hooghly, North 24 Parganas, and Nadia districts, housing roughly 70 of India's 95 operating composite jute mills.
catchment: Catchment Areas: Nadia, Murshidabad, North 24 Parganas, and Hooghly; rail receipts of un-baled and kutcha-baled fiber from North Bengal, Bihar, and Assam.

paragraphs.text: Strategic Role: The global manufacturing center for woven jute products. Runs along both banks of the Hooghly river through Howrah, Hooghly, North 24 Parganas, and Nadia districts, housing roughly 70 of India's 95 operating composite jute mills.
Key Centers: Titagarh, Jagaddal, Naihati, Barrackpore, Bhadreswar, Serampore, Bally, Rishra, and Uluberia.

Infrastructure Profile: Full-scale composite mills containing softener machines (emulsion batching), breaker and finisher cards, drawing frames, flyer spinning frames, and high-speed automatic looms; connected directly to Kolkata and Haldia ports for container and breakbulk dispatch.
Catchment Areas: Nadia, Murshidabad, North 24 Parganas, and Hooghly; rail receipts of un-baled and kutcha-baled fiber from North Bengal, Bihar, and Assam.

paragraphs.text: 2. Seemanchal & North Bengal Primary Processing Corridor (Bihar & WB)
Strategic Role: India's largest inland raw-jute aggregation, grading, and pressing network.

Key Facilities: Gulabbagh Mandi (Purnia), Katihar assembling yards, Kishanganj, and Siliguri transshipment yards; over 150 semi-mechanized Kutcha (lightly pressed) and Pucca (180-kg hydraulic) baling presses.
Catchment Areas: Purnia, Katihar, Kishanganj, Araria, Saharsa (Bihar); Uttar Dinajpur, Dakshin Dinajpur, and Malda (West Bengal).

summary.text: In Indian agricultural and industrial economics (Jute Corporation of India / Directorate of Jute Development / ICAR-CRIJAF), Jute (Corchorus olitorius and Corchorus capsularis, the "Golden Fibre" / Pat / Patsan) is the second most vital natural commercial bast fiber in India after cotton. India is the largest producer of raw jute in the world, contributing roughly 55% to 60% of total global raw fiber output, though Bangladesh remains the primary global exporter of manufactured jute goods.

protection.name: Stem Rot & Root Rot (Macrophomina phaseolina)
protection.geography: All-India Jute Belts (Devastating in West Bengal, Bihar, Assam)
protection.impact: Dark brown, water-soaked, sunken lesions appear on stems; lesions enlarge, girdle the stem, and turn black with tiny black pycnidia; leaves wilt and drop; stem breaks at the point of infection; infected fibers become weak, black, and rotten ("shredded bark"); causes 20–40% fiber loss.
protection.passage: Jute & Mesta — source table 143, row 2. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Jute Semilooper (Anomis sabulifera)
protection.impact: Slender green caterpillars feed voraciously on the tender apical leaves and terminal growing shoots; causes branching (side branches develop), destroying the single straight culm and making fiber extraction irregular and tangled; suppresses plant height.
protection.passage: Jute & Mesta — source table 143, row 3. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Yellow Mite (Polyphagotarsonemus latus)
protection.geography: Warm, Dry Pre-Monsoon Spells (Severe in May–June)
protection.impact: Tiny yellowish mites feed on leaf undersides, injecting toxic secretions; leaves curl downward, turn dark green, become brittle, and develop a coppery-bronze blistered look ("copper leaf"); apical growth halts completely.
protection.passage: Jute & Mesta — source table 143, row 4. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Indigo Caterpillar / Bihar Hairy Caterpillar (Spodoptera exigua, Spilarctia obliqua)
protection.impact: Gregarious hairy caterpillars defoliate young seedlings in nursery and broadcast fields; skeletonize leaves, leaving only veins; causes complete loss of young plant stands.
protection.passage: Jute & Mesta — source table 143, row 5. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Black Band Disease (Diplodia corchori)
protection.impact: A velvety black band of fungal pycnidia encircles the middle or lower stem; stem tissues rot and dry up; leaves shed, leaving bare, blackened stems; destroys fiber tenacity completely.
protection.passage: Jute & Mesta — source table 143, row 6. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Fiber Moisture Rot & Spontaneous Heating (Penicillium, Aspergillus)
protection.impact: Raw fiber baled or stacked at  moisture undergoes microbial fermentation; generates internal heat (stack burn), turning golden fibers dark brown, brittle, and un-spinnable; severe fire risk.
protection.passage: Jute & Mesta — source table 143, row 7. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.
